---
title: "Notebook UX Contracts"
---

Public notebooks are a first-class OrPen SC PDK interface. SCGSim owns the
runtime APIs they call and does not keep duplicate notebook source.

## Palace notebook contract

Only `WORKFLOW_ACTION`, `RUN_ID`, and the run root are global controls. Every
other control is placed beside its immediate action in these stages:

```text
Build Component Coupon
-> Configure EPR / Problem
-> Build Mesh
-> Generate Config
-> Prepare Handoff
-> Analyze Returned Run
```

This contract permits Route A or Route B for the current Surface-EPR direction.
It publishes no private component, selector, dimension, screenshot, config,
mesh, receipt, or artifact.

### Valid setter sequence

The following is an API fragment, not a standalone component notebook. Its
inputs (`component`, `stack`, interface specs, net IDs and numerical controls)
must already come from the consumer's explicit model and environment.

```python
from scgsim.palace import ElectrostaticSim

sim = ElectrostaticSim()
sim.set_output_dir(run_dir)
sim.set_geometry(component)
sim.set_stack(stack)
sim.set_vacuum_region(padding=vacuum_padding_um)
sim.set_surface_epr(representation="B", specs=interface_specs)
sim.add_terminal(terminal_label, net_id=signal_net_id)
sim.add_ground(net_id=physical_ground_net_id)
sim.set_electrostatic(
    unassigned_conductor_policy="error",
    exterior_boundary_policy=exterior_policy,
)

# Build Mesh: these controls belong beside this operation.
sim.set_mesh(refined_mesh_size=refined_size_um, max_mesh_size=bulk_size_um)
mesh_path = sim.mesh()

# Generate Config: solver/FEM/AMR controls belong beside this operation.
sim.set_numerical(**numerical_controls)
config_path = sim.write_config()

# Prepare Handoff: this does not launch Palace or submit a job.
handoff = sim.prepare_handoff(
    profile=launch_profile,
    executable=palace_executable,
    resources=resources,
    setup_commands=setup_commands,
)
```

`set_stack()` must precede `set_surface_epr()`. Supply all geometry-affecting
choices before `mesh()`, including `set_indium_ground_bumps(...)` if used.
`set_airbox(...)` and `set_vacuum_region(...)` are mutually exclusive. A
geometry/stack/route/mesh change invalidates the mesh, config and handoff;
configuration changes invalidate the config and handoff. Regenerate downstream
artifacts into a fresh run rather than editing a sealed file in place.

For `EigenmodeSim`, use the same stages with
`set_eigenmode(num_modes=..., target=..., tolerance=..., save=...)` and
`add_port(name, layer=..., layout_sheet=True, inductance=...)` before mesh.
Here `target` is in **Hz** and inductance in **H**, not the GHz units used by
AEDT run controls. The port refers to authored layout geometry; it is not an
inferred connector. Electrostatic terminals and Eigenmode ports are different
public contracts.

Route A keeps `representation="A"` and additionally requires
`route_a_thin_film="substrate_face"` or `"metal_gap_equivalent"`. Route B
rejects that option. The exact physical/normalized meaning and single-face
constraints are in the [Palace specification](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd).

Notebooks may set `amr_max_passes` (Palace `MaxIts`) and
`amr_nonconformal` (Palace `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal`).
`write_config()` always emits the `Nonconformal` key. The SCGSim default is
`false` so generated configs do not inherit Palace's `true` default. Set
`amr_nonconformal=True` only to opt into nonconformal AMR. Do not delete the
key from a generated config.

`prepare_handoff()` owns `run_palace.sbatch` / `run_palace.sh`. The `profile`
argument is `direct-local`, `slurm-single-node`, or `slurm-multi-node`.
Slurm jobs write stdout and stderr only to `logs/palace-%j.log`. Do not keep a
duplicate `slurm-%j.out`.

`## Analyze Returned Run` uses three separate report families: run identity and
AMR evidence through `show_run_trustworthiness()`, cost/resources through
`show_simulation_benchmark()`, then physics through `show_physics_quantities()`.
`show_all_results()` displays these three exactly once in that order and
returns `None`. Physics-result figures are not the first notebook view.
`resolve_palace_result()` remains strict and accepts completed runs only;
`inspect_run_trustworthiness()` represents failed or partial runs without
changing their receipt status. When the final primary table is missing or
unreadable, inspection selects the latest readable `iterationNN`, records its
source and receipt integrity, and lets the same `show_*` surfaces display it as
partial evidence. Failure diagnosis is independent: a hash-verified Slurm OOM
marker confirms out-of-memory, while exit 137 alone is reported only as a
signal kill. Numerical Evidence plots each readable AMR scalar as its own
figure. AMR error Norm, Maximum, and Mean share one log plot; Minimum is
omitted. Legends sit to the right of each figure. `show_run_trustworthiness()`
and `inspect_run_trustworthiness()` accept `theme="light"` (default) or
`theme="dark"` for Plotly figures only. Identity cards, status cards, and
tables follow the notebook theme. Simulation Benchmark keeps attempted-run
and selected-snapshot cost data and also records per-AMR-pass wall time, DOFs,
and seconds per million DOFs so later runs can accumulate cost statistics.

### Analyze without re-executing

These fragments require an existing returned package; neither invokes a solver:

```python
from scgsim.palace import inspect_run_trustworthiness, resolve_palace_result

# Completed, failed or partial: preserve receipt truth and selected source.
report = inspect_run_trustworthiness(run_dir)
report.show_all_results(theme="light", ranking_limit=20, show_details=False)

# Completed only: also bind the expected handoff identity explicitly.
result = resolve_palace_result(run_dir, expected_handoff_id=handoff_id)
result.show_all_results(theme="light", ranking_limit=20, show_details=False)
```

These are alternative loading paths, not a requirement to load twice. Raw
solver-native parsed tables remain in `result.tables`. `show_details=True`
opts into full provenance/metadata; the readable benchmark object's `.data`
remains available for programmatic access. A partial selection does not become
a completed run, and a hash mismatch is not a reason to bypass the resolver.

### Single runs and sweeps

Only artifact-producing stages need a fresh `RUN_ID` and fresh output location.
Analysis intentionally reads an existing immutable package. A sweep repeats
the same staged contract with explicit ordered parameters, units, case IDs
and failure policy. Never silently discard failed cases or pool distinct modes,
excitations, reference definitions, or alternative mask margins. SCGSim does
not currently provide a generic sweep aggregation or continuation engine;
the consumer owns the case loop without reimplementing runtime/report logic.

## AEDT notebook contract

AEDT examples use the same stage-local rule. Backend-specific setup remains
visible, but handoff construction, execution, native readback, hashes, and
result resolution stay in `scgsim.aedt`, not notebook-local helper code.

Use family-specific immutable specs (`HfssDrivenSpec`, `HfssEigenmodeSpec`,
`Q3dSpec`, `Q2dSpec`) rather than setting native AEDT properties in the notebook.
Keep geometry, materials, ports/nets, setup/convergence, execution and results
visibly distinguishable; the consuming repository chooses its actual cells.

```python
from scgsim.aedt import prepare_handoff, resolve_results

# spec is a fully specified family-specific model; output_dir must not exist.
handoff = prepare_handoff(spec=spec, output_dir=fresh_run_dir)

# Only after separately authorized native execution has completed:
result = resolve_results(returned_run_dir)
physics_rows = result.physics_results()
native_or_primary_artifact = result.primary_csv
convergence = result.convergence
benchmark = result.simulation_benchmark()
```

`prepare_handoff()` does not open AEDT. Running its `run_aedt.sh` is a distinct
explicit execution action requiring AEDT and a license. Unlike Palace
inspection, AEDT `resolve_results()` accepts only completed receipt-bound
packages; it does not provide Palace's partial-report object or `show_*` API.
Do not invent a shared report call across the two families.

## Read-only consumer review checklist

- Check installed version, actual public call signatures and backend status.
- Check geometry/stack/problem/mesh/config/handoff order and direct controls.
- Bind PDK facts and component semantics; do not infer nets, ports, materials,
  or references from names, bounding boxes, physical tags, or render colors.
- Distinguish prepare, execute, analyze, and any explicitly supported reuse.
- Use package parsers, index maps and reports; do not patch solver config,
  normalize solver tables locally, classify failures locally, or import
  historical gsim/external SGB as a runtime fallback.
- Review case identity, units, references and baseline/masked EPR separation.
- Preserve consumer pairing, cell IDs, metadata and Human outputs. Clearing
  outputs or re-executing a notebook requires that repository's authorization.
- Notebook formatting/audit success proves neither native compatibility nor
  mesh quality, convergence, solver agreement or scientific acceptance.
